description:
Retro-Amiga brings the Commodore Amiga to iPad, built on Amiberry, the emulator behind most of the Amiga handhelds and single-board machines people actually play on.

LOAD WHAT YOU ALREADY HAVE
Floppy images (ADF, ADZ, IPF, DMS, SCP, FDI), hard drives (HDF, HDZ, VHD), CD images (ISO, CUE, CHD) and WHDLoad archives (LHA, LZX). Drop files in through the Files app or open them in from anywhere on your iPad. Zipped downloads work as they are, with no unpacking.

WHDLOAD, SET UP FOR YOU
Install WHDLoad once and the app handles the rest, so a downloaded LHA starts the way it was meant to rather than dropping you at a Workbench prompt.

A LIBRARY THAT ORGANISES ITSELF
Everything you import is catalogued automatically, with artwork and a history of what you have been playing.

PICK YOUR AMIGA
A500, A1200, CD32 and more, chosen from a guided setup rather than a wall of options. Configurations are saved, so switching machines takes one tap.

SAVE STATES
The emulator writes a state on the way out, so Resume picks up exactly where you stopped.

CONTROLS YOU CAN MOVE
On-screen joystick, CD32 pad and Amiga keyboard, laid out for touch. The pad designer lets you drag every button where your thumbs actually are, and MFi and Bluetooth controllers are supported throughout.

MOD MUSIC
Import tracker modules (MOD, MED, XM, S3M, IT) and they play in the launcher's own replayer, so the music is there while you browse. None are included; the Music tab starts empty.

IMPORTANT: KICKSTART ROMS ARE NOT INCLUDED
Like every Amiga emulator, this app needs a Kickstart ROM to start. Kickstarts are still under copyright and cannot be distributed with the app, so you supply your own: Cloanto sell them as Amiga Forever, and if you own an Amiga you may already have one. The app scans for what you provide and files it in the right place.

Without a Kickstart the emulator will not boot. Please make sure you can supply one before installing.
promotionalText: A real Amiga on your iPad: floppies, hard drives, WHDLoad and CD32, with save states, a library that organises itself, and controls you can move.
